title: Publication ban imposed at inquest of man involved in confrontation with police
article: Vancouver regional coroner Jeannine Robinson ordered a publication ban Tuesday concerning an issue that has arisen at the inquest into the death of Jeffrey Michael Berg.
Under the terms of the publication ban, media are allowed to report only that there is a ban, but nothing else.

"I would have no problem with the media reporting that we are dealing with sensitive and important matters concerning the continuation of this inquest," said Robinson in granting the application for the ban.
"I believe this is very rare. I don't know if it's unprecedented, but it's very rare," said lawyer Michael Skene, who opposed the application for CTV. "I don't recall any circumstance like this."

Robinson's decision came during the fifth day of the inquest, which has heard dramatic testimony from an eyewitness concerning the confrontation between Berg and Vancouver police Const. David Bruce- Thomas on the night of October 22, 2000.

On Friday, Sari Fujikawa told the four-man, one-woman jury that Berg was standing still, with his hands spread on the trunk of a car in an east side Vancouver alley, when a Vancouver police officer struck him from behind with his gun, then kicked him twice in the back of the neck as he lay on the ground. Berg died two days later in hospital from a heart attack caused by an aneurysm.
The inquest is scheduled to conclude July 9.
